findings.note: parseGitVersion returns whatever token follows the literal word "version", so non-version output that happens to contain that word yields a bogus Version string. "not a version banner" parses to "banner"; gitStatus then only rejects it because atLeastVersion's strconv.Atoi fails, and the reported action reads "...found banner." The gitversion_test "unparseable" case therefore passes through the wrong branch, and parseGitVersion's `return ""` line is never exercised (go tool cover: parseGitVersion 80.0%). A digit-prefix check on the candidate would close both.

A too-old git is reported but never affects any readiness signal: missingFullMetaswarmPrereqs only looks at Present flags, StandaloneReadiness.FullMetaswarmDescription still says "advisory review can run with git and Go", and `metareview setup --check` prints the JSON report and exits 0. An operator scripting on exit status or on fullMetaswarmReady sees a clean setup and then hits the FSM failure the check was added to prevent; only the free-text Action / versionOk fields carry the warning.

The new 1 MiB read cap is one-sided: ReadJSONL now rejects any line longer than maxJSONLLineBytes, but AppendJSONL enforces no matching write-side cap, and a JSONL file is read as a whole. One oversized row (e.g. a long ingested escalationReason on a runs.jsonl record) makes every subsequent ReadJSONL of that file return bufio.ErrTooLong, losing the entire run chain rather than the one row. Capping or rejecting at write time, or skipping over-long lines on read, would keep the failure local.

The cap constant and its five-line comment are duplicated verbatim in internal/state and internal/runchain, and a third JSONL reader sizes its buffer differently: internal/fsm/record/record.go:156 uses sc.Buffer(make([]byte,0,1<<20), 1<<20) with no +2, so a line of exactly 1 MiB that state and runchain admit is rejected there. Rubric duplication concern: one exported cap plus a shared newJSONLScanner helper would make the three readers agree by construction.

Parent-context cancellation is audited as a spawn failure. execRunner returns ctx.Err() unchanged (cmdexec.go:250-252), but in Guarded.exec errs.Code(context.Canceled) is empty, so the err!=nil branch stamps data.Error = ERR_CMD_FAILED and rewrites the error as ERR_CMD_FAILED{reason: "spawn"}. The audited cmd_call for an operator-cancelled or shutdown-cancelled run is thus indistinguishable from a process that failed to start. The underlying error is preserved via errs.Wrap, so errors.Is still works; only the audit record and the surfaced code are wrong.

Suspected env escape: Guarded.env appends the workflow-declared names after MRV_RUN_ID and the {PATH,HOME,LANG,TMPDIR} base, and exec's last-wins semantics would let a declared name shadow the run id or PATH. Checked and refuted: workflow validation rejects those names outright (reservedEnv plus the MRV_/LD_/DYLD_/GIT_ prefixes), so no consented cmd can declare them.

Suspected rubric violation: sharded_test.go assembles the strings "TO"+"DO" and "eval"+"(" at run time, which is exactly the shape of lint evasion the task-done rubric blocks on. Refuted: these are test fixtures that must contain the markers to prove the lints run over the full branch diff, the concatenation is documented in a comment at the constants, and no marker is introduced into shipped source.
